Construction worker nabbed for stabbing friend in QC. A 39-year-old construction worker was arrested after allegedly stabbing his friend during a heated confrontation on Commonwealth Avenue near Don Fabian Street in Barangay Commonwealth, Quezon City, on Aug. 19. The suspect, identified as alias “Mark,” a resident of Barangay Fairview, allegedly asked a witness to accompany him to the area to fetch their friend, who was later identified as the victim, Batasan Police Station (PS 6) said. The witness, who was unaware that the suspect was carrying a knife, agreed to accompany him. Upon reaching the area, the suspect and the victim allegedly got into a heated confrontation, during which the suspect drew a knife and stabbed him. The victim managed to parry the attack but sustained a stab wound to his left arm, while the suspect fled. PS 6 operatives conducted a follow-up operation that led to the suspect’s arrest at around 1:40 p.m. on Aug. 20. Police also recovered an 11-inch kitchen knife with a black-and-red handle believed to have been used in the attack. The victim was brought to Rosario Maclang Bautista General Hospital, where he remains confined. Police records showed that the suspect had previous cases involving physical injuries, violation of Republic Act No. 9262, grave threats, and resistance and disobedience to a person in authority in March 2020; violation of Republic Act No. 9165 in September 2020; and P.D. 1602 in February 2025. The suspect will be charged with frustrated murder before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office.

Belo Medical Group celebrates a new chapter in beauty and longevity. Many of us now pay as much attention to how we feel as to how we look. Looking good still matters, of course. But so do sleeping well, having enough energy, managing stress, and taking care of ourselves as we age. These were among the concerns that led Belo Medical Group to open Xiglo, its first aesthetics and wellness clinic. Dr. Vicki Belo welcomed friends, doctors, and colleagues when the clinic opened recently at 1 Proscenium in Rockwell. Among the guests were Anne Curtis, Solenn Heussaff, Catriona Gray, Gabbi Garcia, Karylle Yuzon, Bianca Gonzalez, Bea Windorski, BJ Pascual, Bea Soriano, Martine Ho, Bianca Henares, Kiana Valenciano, Cristalle Belo-Pitt, Bubbles Paraiso, Mari Jasmine, and Mond Gutierrez. Also present were Dr. Hayden Kho Jr., Belo Medical Group CEO Gina Lorenzana, and longevity consultant Prof. Dr. Dominik Thor. The event gave guests a look at Belo’s move into wellness and precision longevity, something the group had been studying for several years. “We’ve wanted to move into longevity for a few years now,” said Belo. She explained that the group took its time researching the field and consulting experts before opening the clinic. “We really don’t do anything halfway.” Visits to Xiglo are by appointment, with separate rooms for aesthetic treatments and wellness services. A personal concierge guides each client throughout the visit. Precision longevity may sound like a complicated term, but the idea is simple. It looks at how each person is aging, taking into account medical history, lifestyle, test results, and personal goals. Doctors then prepare an individual plan instead of recommending the same program for everyone. The clinic developed its program with Dr. Dominik Thor, president of the Geneva College of Longevity Science and Belo Medical Group’s longevity consultant. A visit starts with a consultation with a precision longevity physician. Diagnostic tests may then be recommended to establish the client’s baseline. “We listened to our patients, and what they were asking for changed,” said Belo Medical Group chief executive officer Gina Lorenzana. “People still care about aesthetics, and we’re very good at that. But now they’re also concerned about what’s happening on the inside.”

SC affirms conviction of a man for ‘arbitrarily, publicly’ withdrawing license to marry his pregnant girlfriend. The Supreme Court (SC) has affirmed the conviction for psychological violence of a man who first reneged on his commitment to secure a license to marry a lady teacher he impregnated in 2020, withdrew the license when it was finally filed, and later married another woman. Upheld by the SC was the conviction of the man for inflicting psychological trauma on the teacher in violation of Republic Act No. 9262, the Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act (VAWC) of 2004. The SC, however, modified the penalty imposed by the Court of Appeals (CA) which upheld the ruling meted out by the regional trial court (RTC). It imposed on the man a jail term of two years, four months and one day as minimum to nine years and four months as maximum. He was also ordered to pay the teacher P75,000 in moral damages and P75,000 in exemplary damages with six percent interest annually until fully paid. The names of the parties in the case docketed as GR No. E-00648 were redacted by the SC in the decision written by Associate Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando and posted on the SC website – sc.judiciary.gov.ph – last August 17. The CA had ruled that the man “was not being penalized for the breach of promise to marry itself, but for the consequential effects of his actions that led to the teacher being humiliated and publicly ridiculed.” It also rejected the man’s contention that his act “was innocent, considering he knew the negative emotional effects his actions would cause the teacher and the scandal it would bring to her as a public- school teacher.” In denying the petition filed by the man, the SC said that his arguments were laced with questions of fact and attempted to circumvent the rule by seeking a recalibration of the evidence already evaluated by the RTC and the CA. It said the appeal claimed the lower courts misapprehended the facts and improperly applied the provisions of RA 9262 by convicting him for a breach of promise to marry and for expanding the application of the law to non-abusive or failed relationships resulting from incompatibility. However, the SC said that RA 9262 “focuses on the effect of the offender's acts -- specifically the mental or emotional anguish caused to a woman with whom the offender had a sexual or dating relationship.” “Since the lady teacher was pregnant and the withdrawal of the marriage application was done ‘arbitrarily’ and ‘publicly’ at the Local Civil Registrar, the act transcends simple heartbreak and enters the realm of ‘psychological violence,’” it also said. At the same time, the SC rejected the man’s claim of “improper expansion” of RA 9262. “The law is a protective statute; where an act -- even one involving marriage applications -- is used as a tool to inflict psychological trauma on a woman in a dating or sexual relationship, the law must be interpreted to hold the offender liable. The RTC and the CA did not penalize the petitioner for the breach of promise to marry itself. Section 5(i) of RA 9262 specifically penalizes acts that cause mental or emotional suffering,” the SC pointed out. It noted that the RTC, as upheld by the CA, penalized the man because his "willful" withdrawal of the marriage license -- knowing that the teacher was pregnant and had already announced the union – “constitutes a form of emotional manipulation and public humiliation that fits the definition of psychological violence.” The SC ruled: “Finally, the penalties of fine and the requirement of mandatory counseling, are all proper and in accordance with the law. The same applies to the grant of moral and exemplary damages, as these awards are supported by factual basis and prevailing jurisprudence. However, the penalty of imprisonment must be modified. Petitioner is sentenced to suffer the penalty of two years, four months and one day of prision correccional, as minimum, to nine years and four months of prision mayor, as maximum.”

2 laborers arrested for illegal drugs in Taguig. Police arrested a construction worker and a carpenter for illegal drugs in two operations in Taguig City on Thursday, Aug. 20. Personnel of the Taguig Police Station Drug Enforcement Unit nabbed a listed street-level drug suspect and seized over P152,320 worth of shabu during a buy-bust operation on C-5 Road in Barangay Fort Bonifacio. Police identified the suspect as alias “Eric,” 26, a construction worker and resident of Barangay Fort Bonifacio. The operation was conducted at a mini park near the C-5 Road overpass, where an undercover officer acted as a poseur-buyer and transacted with the suspect, leading to his arrest. During the operation, police seized seven plastic sachets containing 22.4 grams of shabu, buy-bust money consisting of a genuine P500 bill, and P3,000 in boodle money. The suspect will face a complaint for violation of Sections 5 (sale of dangerous drugs) and 11 (possession of dangerous drugs) of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. In Barangay Central Signal, operatives of the Southern Police District’s District Mobile Force Battalion and Muntinlupa police arrested alias “Rex,” 42, a carpenter listed among the top 10 most wanted persons. He was nabbed based on a warrant of arrest for service of sentence issued on May 26 by Presiding Judge Bernard Bernal of the Taguig Regional Trial Court Branch 70 in connection with a case for violation of Section 14 (possession of drug paraphernalia) of Republic Act 9165. Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco, SPD director, commended the teams for the arrests.

A closer look at Romblon's beaches, heritage sites, underwater wonders, and laid-back island escapes. By NANCY MARIE ANDAM The Philippines is home to no shortage of world-famous beach destinations. From powdery white sands to crystal-clear waters, it's easy to keep returning to the same familiar islands year after year. But some of the country's best escapes are the ones that fly under the radar. Tucked in the heart of the archipelago, Romblon is one of those places. Often overlooked by travelers, the province is known for its pristine beaches, hidden coves, and rich marble industry, which has long been part of its identity. Through a trip led by the Department of Tourism-MIMAROPA, Manila Bulletin Lifestyle was able to explore the historic sites and natural beauty of Romblon. If you're ready to venture beyond the usual beach itinerary, here are some of the must-visit spots that make it worth the trip. Fuerza San Andres Fort San Andres Rd, Romblon, Romblon One of the first places we visited in Romblon was Fuerza San Andres, which sits atop San Antonio Hill overlooking the town and its natural harbor. Built by the Spaniards in 1644 to defend the island against Dutch marauders and Muslim raiders, the fort remains one of the province's most important historical landmarks. It's also one of the perfect places to take in views of the Romblon port and nearby islands. It is best to visit around 4 p.m. to witness the sunset and avoid the heat during the day. Saint Joseph Cathedral Parish Rizal St., Poblacion, Romblon, Romblon Beyond its marble industry, Romblon is also home to historic landmarks like the Romblon Cathedral. Officially known as the Saint Joseph Cathedral Parish, it is the oldest Roman Catholic church in the province. During our visit, we learned that it houses a replica of the Santo Niño de Cebu, enshrined in 1728. Inside, the church's marble details are hard to miss, reflecting the province's long-standing connection to the industry. Its belfry, which once served as a watchtower against incoming invaders, is also a reminder of the church's role in the town's history. Bonbon Beach Romblon Island, Romblon Bonbon Beach is just 3 to 5 km from the town proper and ferry port, and it's easy to see why it earned a spot on The World's 50 Best Beaches list. Its clear waters and long sandbar make it a great place to slow down and take in the scenery. We found that visiting in the late afternoon before sunset was the best time to enjoy a peaceful walk along the sandbar. Cobrador Island Cobrador Island was easily our favorite beach in Romblon. After a 40-minute boat ride from the main port, we were welcomed by one of the bluest oceans we’ve ever seen. The island is known for its crushed-coral white sand beaches, but what stood out to me most was how calm and peaceful it felt. Just off the coast, we also visited Takot Reef, where we got to cliff jump and snorkel. If you're lucky, you might even spot sea turtles in the area. Visitors are charged an environmental fee of around ₱20 to ₱30. There are also basic cottages for around ₱300 where you can leave your things. If you're going island hopping, we would recommend bringing small bills to make paying local fees easier. In our case, we had Papagabs Travel and Tours, which covered the environmental fees needed in our island-hopping activity. Biaringan Islet Biaringan Islet, located at the northeastern end of Tablas Island, was another stop during our trip. The islet has rocky coastlines and clear blue waters, with views of nearby areas including Romblon Island. We also learned that it used to have a zipline, but it has remained closed since the pandemic. Even without it, the islet was a nice place to take in the horizon and enjoy the quieter side of the province. Cawayan Blue Hole Barangay Cawayan, San Agustin, Tablas Island If you're into freediving or scuba diving, the Blue Hole is a must-visit in Tablas Island. You can reach the site by boat, where you're greeted by deep blue water surrounded by rocky cliffs. Beneath the surface, the site opens into a vertical drop lined with coral and sea fans. The entrance is around 5 to 7 meters deep and reaches about 27 to 30 meters on a sloping sandy floor, making it more suitable for experienced divers who are comfortable with deeper waters and possible currents. Above the site stands Gorda Point Lighthouse, a remnant of the American colonial period. We climbed at least 300 steps to reach the top, but the view made the effort worth it, with a wide stretch of ocean and the Blue Hole visible below. Lapus-Lapus Beach Barangay Talisay, Calatrava, Tablas Island Lapus-Lapus Beach, locally known as “Little Palawan,” is one of those spots in Tablas Island that feels worth the journey. From Calatrava Port, we took a 30-minute pump boat ride to Barangay Talisay, where the beach’s golden sand and shallow clear waters welcomed us. The rock formations and corals around the cove reminded us of Palawan, but the quiet surroundings gave it a more laid-back feel. There are no restaurants on the beach, so we would recommend bringing your own food and drinks. You can also rent a cottage for around ₱200. The entrance fee is around ₱25 per person, making it a simple and affordable stop if you’re exploring Tablas Island. Binucot Beach and Bel-at Point Barangay Bunsoran, Ferrol, Tablas Island With its calm shoreline and open view of the sea, Binucot Beach offers a quiet stop in Ferrol. It is roughly a 20-minute drive or tricycle ride south from Odiongan Port. We spent some time by the water, where the clear shallows made it easy to spot coral patches and small marine life while swimming or snorkeling. A short distance from the beach, you'll find Bel-at Point, a rocky cove with a wooden boardwalk that stretches over the water. The area is especially worth visiting in the late afternoon, when the setting sun adds another reason to stay a little longer. Public access to Binucot Beach is generally free, although some resorts may charge for accommodation or day-use amenities. Looc Fish Sanctuary Looc, Tablas Island A 48-hectare protected area in the middle of Looc Bay. Accessible by boat, the sanctuary has an entrance fee of around ₱160 to ₱200. At its floating wooden pontoon, you could look through the viewing deck and see schools of colorful reef fish and giant clams in the clear waters below. We highly suggest trying the fish feeding, especially if you're lucky enough to have more fish gather around you. Don't know how to swim? Life vests are provided, and snorkeling gear is also available for rent if you want to explore the marine life up close. Santa Fe Beaches Santa Fe, known as the “Beach Capital of Romblon,” was one of the areas you can explore on the southern tip of Tablas Island. It has popular beach spots, including Agmanic, Balisa, and Kaburihan, each offering clear waters, white sand, and a quiet island atmosphere. Carabao Island Just a boat ride away from Boracay, Carabao Island offers a quieter escape with plenty to explore. If you're planning a visit, add Said Beach for a peaceful walk along its white sand and turquoise waters, preferably in the morning or late afternoon. For sunset, head to Tagaytay Viewpoint, where you can enjoy views of Boracay and nearby islands from the hilltop tree house. Don't miss Cathedral Cave either, where a 10-minute trek leads to a hidden lagoon with turquoise water. We took a quick dip, which made the trek worth it. If you're feeling adventurous, there's also a cliff-jumping spot nearby. Romblon is the kind of place we suggest taking your time with. Beyond the beaches, there are caves to explore, reefs to discover, historic sites to visit, and quiet corners that make the journey feel worth it. From its natural wonders to the communities and traditions that shape the province, there's more to it than a quick island escape. If you're looking for a destination beyond the usual island stops, put Romblon on your list and let the province surprise you along the way.

Madonna celebrates 68th birthday with family, BF in Greece. Madonna marked her 68th birthday with people closest to her, celebrating with five of her six children and boyfriend Akeem Morris during a getaway to the Greek island of Corfu. The pop superstar gave fans a glimpse of the celebration on Instagram, Aug. 16. Among the photos was of Madonna dressed in an elaborate multicolored Dolce & Gabbana dress, paired with a bright pink floral headpiece and gold accessories. She later changed into a white ensemble as she and her guests continued the celebration. “It’s My Birthday! Eat, Pray, Love, Drink, Dance, Break plates, Feed Cats!! Thank you G*D!” Madonna wrote in the caption. The birthday dinner was held at a traditional taverna in Kouramades, a village in Corfu. The celebration featured Greek music, traditional food and the breaking of plates, a familiar part of Greek festivities. As to the celebrant's cake, it was large, heart-shaped with a white-and-gold evil-eye design. Madonna was photographed blowing out the candles as her children helped bring out the cake. The birthday celebration was part of a longer Greek vacation for the singer, who reportedly spent the week in Corfu with family and friends. The trip included time at sea and a visit to Meteora, the historic complex of monasteries in central Greece. The festivities came at a particularly busy time for Madonna. Earlier this week, she became the leading nominee for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, earning 11 nominations, her highest total in a single year. She also received nominations connected to her collaboration with Sabrina Carpenter, “Bring Your Love.” The 2026 MTV VMAs will air live from Los Angeles on Sept. 27.

Mazda launches all-new 2027 CX-5 HEV. Mazda Philippines has just taken the wraps off the all-new 2027 CX-5. The all-new CX-5 now has a more confident design, enhanced interior comfort, and greater everyday usability. New style The latest generation stays true to its distinctive silhouette while introducing sleek proportions, a bolder presence, and improved everyday functionality. The all-new CX-5’s proportions have been optimized for a more planted and roomier vehicle. Compared to its predecessor, it is longer (+115 mm), wider (+15 mm), and taller (+30 mm). Similarly, its wheelbase has grown (+115 mm) resulting in more cabin space than ever before, particularly in the form of best-in-class second-row legroom. Mazda designers raised the CX-5’s nose to enhance its presence, to give drivers a greater sense of security and a more commanding view of the road. The front wing lines are now easier to see from the driver’s seat, helping with spatial awareness in tighter spaces. The side profile continues Mazda’s Kodo design philosophy, combining organic surface transitions with crisp lines to convey motion and simplicity. Standard on the all-new CX-5 variants are 19-inch alloy wheels with a black metallic finish. It also features gloss black lower cladding creating a strikingly sporty presence. At the rear, new linear LED taillights keep the overall look clean and modern. A hands-free power tailgate is standard. The all-new CX-5 is available in six colors, including the new Navy Blue Mica, introduced for the first time in the Mazda line-up. Other colors are Soul Red Crystal, Rhodium White, Machine Gray, Jet Black, and Aero Gray. A crafted interior Inside, the all-new Mazda CX-5 embodies the principle of Ma, a key pillar of Japanese aesthetics that prioritize space, balance, and harmony. The result is an uncluttered, spacious cabin that is serene and functional, perfect for families, where the driver can focus and the passengers can relax. The driver-oriented environment features a horizontal door-to-door dashboard layout. The driver gets an all-digital 10.25-inch instrument cluster with customizable access to key vehicle information, including ADAS status, navigation cues, and media playback. A head-up display is projected on the front windshield. Clean capacitive steering wheel switches integrate commonly used functions such as Mi-Drive mode selection, media controls, or the camera button for quickly checking the car’s surroundings. In addition to touch-sensitive slide gestures—for example when adjusting volume—the switches also retain familiar rocker-style press operation. It comes with a new integrated 15.6-inch infotainment system taking center stage. The redesigned center console has cupholders and a wireless charger, while longer, better-aligned armrests and refined front seats create a more stable and relaxed posture. The in-car experience boasts of improved safety and connectivity. The intuitive and always-on touchscreen has smartphone-like usability and a customizable home screen with quick access to frequently used features. It provides seamless access to voice assistance for access to popular apps for music, video streaming, and news. The touchscreen system also replaces previously physical controls, such as climate control functions, for a more streamlined layout, and provides an enhanced overview of the surroundings via the 360° View Monitor. The CX-5 comes standard with a Bose 12-speaker premium sound system with Perceptual Sound Rendering (PSR). Behind, knee clearance is increased by 64 mm and headroom by 29 mm. The rear door opening has also been expanded by 70 mm. Combined with a wider scuff plate and lowered hip point, entry and exit are more natural and effortless for occupants of all ages. The extended wheelbase also enhances cargo usability. By increasing load floor depth by approximately 45 mm, bulky items such as luggage can be stored upright, improving flexibility and making better use of the available space. Interior materials and finishes make use of Japanese Sen Wood. High-contact areas are finished in black to minimize visible wear and tear. Genuine sports tan leather seats come with powered front seat adjustment, with memory presets for the driver. Seat ventilation is standard on the all-new CX-5. New ambient lighting comes with a choice of seven colors. A panoramic sunroof makes the all-new CX-5 feel even more spacious and open. The cabin features sound-absorbing and insulating materials in key areas, to keep noise for passengers to an absolute minimum. Precisely tuning the vibration of each component allowed unwanted sounds to be minimized. The updated engine, equipped with a balancer shaft, helps reduce vibrations and low-frequency noise. Effortless control Mazda is committed to the joy of driving, and the Jinba Ittai feeling of oneness between car and driver. To support this, Mazda revised the suspension setup with softer springs, adjusted the size of anti-roll bars and carefully tuned the dampers to better absorb road irregularities. This provides better control and road-holding, especially during faster cornering, while still ensuring a smooth and stable ride. It also more effectively absorbs vibrations from uneven road surfaces, improving overall comfort. The steering feel has been refined to offer a lighter, more intuitive handling while maintaining accurate feedback from the vehicle. The pedal response has also been optimized to allow drivers to experience swifter, more predictable feedback, and consistent acceleration without delays. Powering the all-new CX-5 is a new 2.5-liter e-Skyactiv-G coupled with the Mazda hybrid system. This combination delivers a more efficient and responsive engine, while retaining the mechanical purity and direct feedback. The engine output and torque peak at 181-PS and 242-Nm. For the first time, the all-new Mazda CX-5 introduces full hybrid technology, bringing greater efficiency and refinement to the driving experience. The system works seamlessly with the engine to support smoother acceleration and deceleration, helping optimize fuel efficiency while maintaining the responsive and engaging drive that Mazda is known for. The engine is mated to a recalibrated six-speed automatic transmission. It has been programed for reduced shift frequency and smoother or crisper transitions depending on load and the driver’s preference. Enhanced safety Reflecting Mazda’s commitment to advanced safety and driver-support systems, the all-new Mazda CX-5 has achieved the highest level of safety with a five-star rating at the Euro NCAP and ANCAP as well as a Top Safety Pick+ recognition by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). It introduces a comprehensive suite of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) improving safety, awareness, and comfort over a wide range of everyday driving scenarios. The Mazda i-Activsense package includes: Front & Rear Smart Brake Support (SBS), enhanced Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM), Driver Monitoring and Driver Attention Alert, Cruising and Traffic Support (CTS) with Lane Change Assist (LCA), and Mazda Radar Cruise Control (MRCC) with Emergency Lane Keeping (ELK). “Since Bermaz Auto Philippines took over the exclusive distributorship of Mazda in the Philippines, the CX-5 has been a core part of our line-up. Known for its distinctive design and responsive performance, it is the choice for drivers seeking a refined yet practical compact SUV,” said Steven Tan, Mazda Philippines President and CEO. “Now on its third generation, the all-new Mazda CX-5 combines a more intuitive human-machine interface with the same emotional appeal that defines the brand expressed through Jinba-Ittai driving dynamics and Kodo design, while enhancing everyday comfort through improved packaging and ride quality. It meets the demands of daily commuting while remaining versatile enough for weekend travel or family use.” The all-new CX-5 is offered in a single 2.5L AWD HEV Premium Plus variant, priced at P2,495,000. A FWD HEV variant will be offered next year. The price includes a three-year bumper-to-bumper warranty and a complimentary five-year service plan, providing customers with greater peace of mind and an elevated ownership experience. The all-new CX-5 is on display this weekend at the North Court at the Powerplant Mall in Rockwell, Makati. Visitors can see the new model and place reservations if desired.

Charly Suarez title shot in jeopardy as Navarrete enters unification with Foster. Charly Suarez’s long-awaited world title shot is facing yet another uncertainty as Mexican super featherweight champion Emanuel Navarrete entered talks of a possible unification bout with fellow titlists O’Shaquie Foster. According to multiple reports, Navarrete and Foster have already verbally agreed to the unification which would stake the former’s World Boxing Organization and International Boxing Federation belts and the latter’s World Boxing Council strap. Navarrete’s camp had also already reached out to the WBO to formally allow him to stake his belt for the bout despite the body’s current order for him to fight No. 1 contender in Suarez. “I believe the committee will render a decision pursuant to the WBO’s policies, rules and regulations, while serving the best interests of boxing,” said WBO president Gustavo Olivieri. The Navarrete-Foster three-belt unification was reportedly penciled on Oct. 24 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. Should the Mexican champion get the green light, it would mean that Suarez will have to wait further before finally getting the rematch he has long wanted following the controversial no-contest outcome against Navarrete in their first fight. It will also be the second time that Suarez will give way for Navarrete’s unification bid after also allowing the Mexican to go for the blockbuster bout against the former IBF champion Eduardo Nunez. Suarez, on the other hand, in an effort to stay in shape for the title shot, fought and defeated Manuel Avila with a first-round knockout win.

'Napipikon na sila': Adiong details Kapunan's effect on Duterte camp. Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong totally understands why the camp of impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte hates private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan so much. For one thing, Kapunan has been killing it--so to speak--in the Senate impeachment trial in terms of buttressing the case against the Vice President. “Mas lalong klarong lumalabas na mas napipikon na sila sa mga katulad ni Atty. Kapunan na magagaling na mga abogado at mas epektibo sa paglalahad ng mga testimonya ng mga witnesses na hindi nasasagot diretsa ng depensa,” Adiong said during an online press briefing. (It is becoming clearer that they are getting more irritated with lawyers like Atty. Kapunan, who are skilled and more effective in presenting witness testimonies that the defense cannot directly answer.) The prosecution panel spokesperson was alluding to Davao City 1st district Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte, who called Kapunan the “Marites ng impeachment (Rumor source of the impeachment)” and criticized her for linking the Duterte family to what she described as a "culture of violence" . “Isa lang masasabi ko, kaya ata nila sini-single out ngayon si Atty. Kapunan kasi talagang magaling siya. She was able to elicit information from the witnesses that strengthened the case against the Vice President,” Adiong pointed out. (The only thing I can say is that maybe they are singling out Atty. Kapunan now because she is truly skilled. She was able to elicit information from the witnesses that strengthened the case against the Vice President.) Kapunan--who has nearly 50 years of law practice experience under her belt--leads the 15 private prosecutors that are helping the House prosecution panel gain a conviction on the respondent. Kapunan had earlier said following the deadly Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting that Vice President’s words and actions were contributing to what she described as a culture of violence in the country. While Kapunan wasn't blaming the Vice President alone for violence in the country, she said the latter was being part of the problem rather than the solution. To this, Adiong said: “I’m not gonna defend Atty. Kapunan because she can ably defend herself." Personal attacks won't cut it But he reckoned that personal attacks like those from Rep. Duterte would neither help respondent Duterte’s defense nor answer the allegations against her. “Personal attacks, saying na 'marites', will not help not only the case of the defense, but it will not help the entirety of the proceedings by focusing on the merits of the case,” said the Lanao del Sur solon. Kapunan has taken a prominent role in examining witnesses on Duterte’s alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds at the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd). Adiong said attacking Kapunan over her opinions or personality would not answer the questions raised by the evidence presented in the impeachment trial. “It will not be a way to counter the allegations, much less provide an answer to the increasing questions surrounding the misuse of the confidential funds of the OVP."

NHCP leads rites marking Ninoy Aquino’s martyrdom at NAIA. The National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) led the commemoration of the 43rd anniversary of the assassination of former Senator Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Jr. at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 1 in Parañaque City on Friday morning, Aug. 21. NHCP Chair Regalado Trota Jose Jr. offered flowers at the site where Aquino was gunned down on August 21, 1983. He was joined by representatives from the New NAIA Infrastructure Corporation, Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA), Human Rights Violations Victims’ Memorial Commission, Spirit of EDSA Foundation, Bantayog ng mga Bayani Foundation, Project Gunita, August Twenty-One Movement, Chino Roces Foundation, NAMSERV, and Earthsaver. “This simple ceremony is a reminder of the sacrifice that helped awaken the nation to the struggle for democracy,” Jose said during the rites. Aquino, a leading critic of then President Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr., was among the first opposition figures arrested after Martial Law was declared in September 1972. He spent eight years in detention, where he staged a 40-day hunger strike in 1975 to protest military court proceedings. In 1980, after suffering a heart attack in prison, he was allowed to leave for medical treatment abroad. Jose recalled that Aquino returned to the Philippines in 1983 despite threats to his life. “His decision to come home showed his commitment to the Filipino people,” he said. Aquino was shot dead upon arrival at the airport, an event that galvanized calls for reform and drew millions to his funeral procession. The NHCP noted that Aquino’s death became a turning point that fueled the 1986 People Power Revolution. Republic Act No. 9256 later declared August 21 as Ninoy Aquino Day, a special non-working holiday. Senator Bam Aquino also sent a wreath that was placed beside the monument earlier in the day. “This annual commemoration ensures that the memory of Ninoy Aquino’s sacrifice continues to inspire future generations,” Jose added.

Julie Anne San Jose remembers Vanessa Blanca. For Julie Anne San Jose, the sudden passing of fellow singer Vanessa Blanca was a deeply personal loss, given their shared history. The two were members of Sugarpop during their formative years, alongside Rita Daniela, Enzo Almario, and Cholo Bismonte. Following the news of Vanessa’s passing, Julie Anne took to Instagram to pay tribute to her friend. Record $5.5M payday awaits US Open singles champions. NEW YORK (AP) — The U.S. Open singles champions will earn $5.5 million, the highest winnings in Grand Slam tennis history. Overall compensation for the final major of the year is rising to a record $108 million, a 20% increase from last year and a 44% jump since 2024. The financial details were announced Thursday, Aug. 20, by the U.S. Tennis Association, with play set to begin next week. Players will earn $140,000, largest in tennis history, just for making it into the 128-player singles main draw. A quarterfinalist earns $780,000, a semifinalist $1.45 million and the runner-up $2.8 million. The champions' check is up from the $5 million that Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz won last year, when the total player compensation was $90 million. The winning teams in men's, women's and mixed doubles will split $1 million, with the runner-up team to earn $500,000. The wheelchair singles champions will earn $104,000. The USTA also announced it would establish a player support program, with an initial commitment of $2 million to be split equally between men's and women's players, which will be used to provide benefits and complement existing pension funds. USTA CEO Craig Tiley called the financial commitment to players at all levels a “significant first step in a multiyear investment in athletes as the U.S. Open continues to be the best economic opportunity for players and the most valuable platform in tennis for players, fans and partners.” The program will be designed with guidance from the Grand Slam Player Council, whose creation was announced Thursday in response to players seeking greater input and revenue from the four major tournaments.

Philippine insurance premiums surpass ₱280 million on strong life demand. The Philippine insurance sector recorded a robust performance in the first six months of 2026, surpassing ₱280 billion in total premium collections, fueled by increased public demand for financial protection and strong sales of life insurance products. According to the latest data released by the Insurance Commission (IC) on Aug. 20, combined premium collections across life and non-life insurance companies, as well as mutual benefit associations (MBAs), grew by 16.2 percent year-on-year. Total collections reached ₱282.9 billion as of end-June, up from ₱243.39 billion in the same period last year. According to the IC, the increase in collections lifted the country’s overall insurance penetration—the ratio of total insurance premiums collected to gross domestic product (GDP)—to 1.96 percent, up 0.16 percentage points from the 1.80 percent recorded in mid-2025. These indicators drove the regulator’s optimism over the domestic insurance landscape. The IC said the results are encouraging and point to “rising public awareness of financial protection, greater insurance adoption, and growing confidence in the insurance industry.” Further, the IC said the increase in insurance penetration was “attributable to the substantial increase in premium collections by insurance companies.” Life insurance continued to lead the sector’s expansion, accounting for the lion’s share of total collections. Life insurers posted a 17.9 percent increase in collections, climbing to ₱230 billion by midyear from ₱195.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Variable life insurance products, such as investment-linked policies, drove the growth in life insurance, increasing by 14.8 percent to ₱150 billion. Meanwhile, traditional life insurance products posted a 24.3 percent increase, rising from ₱64.4 billion in 2025 to ₱80 billion in 2026. Other segments of the local insurance landscape also recorded solid gains. Non-life insurance net premiums written climbed by 10 percent to ₱44.2 billion as of end-June, from ₱40.2 billion a year earlier. MBAs recorded total contributions and premiums of ₱8.7 billion, posting 7.1 percent growth from the ₱8.2 billion collected in the comparable period a year earlier. Individually, Filipinos are also dedicating more resources to insurance. The country’s insurance density—the average amount spent by each individual on insurance—increased by 15.2 percent to ₱2,469 from ₱2,142 in mid-2025. Payouts also surged during the period, with total benefits reaching ₱90.9 billion, up 16.7 percent from the benefits paid a year earlier and more than double the total benefits disbursed in the first quarter of the year. Even with substantial payouts, the industry’s aggregate balance sheet remained resilient. Total assets expanded by 8.5 percent to ₱2.76 trillion, while total net worth rose four percent to ₱515.6 billion. Total paid-up capital and guaranty fund increased 2.4 percent to ₱87.4 billion, while total liabilities grew 9.6 percent year-on-year to ₱2.25 trillion. (Derco Rosal)

Mother, 2 children found dead inside car in Bulacan. A woman and her two young children were found dead inside a car in a remote vacant lot in Barangay Talacsan, San Rafael, Bulacan, on Thursday afternoon, Aug. 20. Police said they received a report at 2:11 p.m. from a concerned citizen about a suspicious silver vehicle abandoned in the area. Authorities immediately responded and, upon checking the vehicle, were shocked to discover three bodies in the back of the multipurpose vehicle (MPV). Police said the victims were residents of Baliwag City. The father told investigators he last saw his family at 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, Aug. 19. The mother was 31 years old, while the children were aged nine and four. The Philippine National Police Forensic Group is conducting a thorough investigation into the incident. As of press time, authorities have not yet determined the cause of death.

GAC launches GS4 Max HEV. GAC Motor has just launched the GAC GS4 Max HEV, a next-generation hybrid SUV. The GS4 MAX delivers a high-value blend of maximum space, comfort, safety, and efficiency. Powering the vehicle is GAC’s 2.0L Atkinson-cycle dedicated hybrid engine paired with a two-speed Dedicated Hybrid Transmission (DHT) and a 2.1 kWh Nickel Cobalt Manganese (NCM) battery. Combining modern architectural aesthetics with GAC’s advanced hybrid technology, the multi-mode system seamlessly transitions between Pure Electric (EV), Hybrid (HV), Direct Engine Drive, and Energy Recuperation modes. Powered by an Atkinson-cycle HEV engine, the system achieves a combined power output of 232-HP and a maximum motor torque of 300-N·m. Designed to optimize output while minimizing fuel consumption, it delivers an outstanding total combined driving range of up to 1,250-kilometers on a single tank, offering electric vehicle-like responsiveness with long-range peace of mind for daily city commutes and weekend getaways. Family-ready space and comfort Tailored specifically for family-oriented users, the cabin is thoughtfully designed to maximize spatial freedom and passenger comfort on every journey. On the tech front, driver control is centered around a 10.1-inch Multifunctional Touchscreen compatible with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a 7-inch LCD Digital Instrument Cluster, an aircraft-inspired gear selector, and a 50W Wireless Smartphone Charger with built-in cooling fan technology. Externally, its clean, confident presence is framed by a bold Qilin-inspired front fascia, Qingyun Ladder matrix grille, Morning Star LED headlights, full-width Changhong LED taillights, and electric hidden door handles. Thanks to a generous 2,750 mm wheelbase and an expansive 1,901 mm wide body profile, the GS4 MAX HEV provides class-leading legroom and shoulder room across both rows. The interior features a modern minimalist black cabin crafted for low-maintenance elegance, framed by an expansive panoramic glass roof with an electric sunshade that bathes the space in natural light. Passengers benefit from zero-pressure comfort seats with precision piping and extensive perforation for superior long-distance support. Designed around real-world family needs, the cabin incorporates whisper-quiet acoustic insulation, rear passenger air vents, and smart storage compartments throughout. When maximum cargo capacity is required, the second-row seats fold completely flat to unlock a seamless, unobstructed load floor. Advanced safety, smart tech Built around a robust safety-cage body structure comprising high-strength and ultra-high-strength steel in critical load-bearing areas, protection is further anchored by an Airbag Protection System equipped with dual front, front side, second-row side airbags, and seamless one-piece woven side curtain airbags. Driving confidence is elevated by a full Level 2 Driver Assistance Suite, including Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), Forward Collision Warning (FCW), Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB-VRU), Traffic Jam Assist (TJA), Lane Keep Assist (LKA), Lane Departure Warning (LDW), and Integrated Cruise Assist (ICA), alongside a Surround View Camera System. The GS4 Max HEV is priced at P1,298,000, but is currently offered at an introductory price of P1,218,000, giving early buyers as much as P80,000 savings. Reservations are now open at GAC dealerships nationwide.
